prerequisites: Mathematical calculus at the technical university graduates level

learning_outcomes.text: Acquaint students with the representation, processing and analysis of continuous signals and systems (filters) used in communication systems and control technology.
Understand representation and modeling of continuous signals and systems.
Utilize tools for the analysis of continuous periodic and non-periodic signals in the time and frequency domain.
Design continuous systems with required characteristics, both by solving differential equations and by Laplace transform.
Describe the state of continuous systems.
Acquire theoretical and practical knowledge from the area of continuous signals processing and analysis in time and frequency domain.
Be familiar with the design of continuous systems according to specific requirements, determining the output of the system (filter design).

syllabus_topics: Mathematical apparatus for continuous signal processing
Representation and classification of signals, characteristics of signals
Operations with continuous signals and basic types of continuous signals (harmonic signals, Dirac pulse, unit jump, pulse signal, triangular signal)
Tools for analysis of continuous periodic signals in the frequency domain (FS)
Tools for analysis of continuous non-periodic signals in the frequency domain (FT)
Continuous systems in the time domain
Description and solution of continuous systems using differential equations
Laplace transform I. (relations, convergence region, properties)
Laplace transform II. (Laplace transform of significant signals, inverse Laplace transform)
Determination of frequency characteristics in continuous systems
Continuous LTI systems (ideal filters and their characteristics, lossless transmission lines)
Design of analogue filters I. (Butterworth filters)
Design of analogue filters II. (Chebyshev filters)
assessment_rules: Attendance rate of at least 80% is required. All homework assignments must be completed. The oral exam consists of three questions, each scoring 1 point, with a minimum of 0.5 points required per question. The final score is based on a scale from A (3-2.7 points) to F (<1.5 points).
degree: Bachelor's programme, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Informatics - courses in English
